features.text: Patient is 62 years old and male.
Patient had a heart attack about six months ago.
Patient is taking aspirin and Brilinta.
Patient takes fish oil.
Patient was on a statin called Crestor before but is unsure if still taking it.
Patient stopped taking Crestor due to muscle aches.
Patient did not see a healthcare provider about the muscle aches from Crestor and stopped it on his own.
Patient has not experienced any new or worsening symptoms since discontinuing Crestor, such as chest pain, shortness of breath, or fatigue.
Patient experiences dizziness when standing up too fast.
Patient has not noticed any changes in exercise tolerance, fatigue, or swelling in his legs since discontinuing Crestor.
Patient has mild puffiness in his legs, which he thinks is related to his medications.
Patient has not noticed any changes in leg swelling or if it has worsened since stopping Crestor.
Patient has not noticed any changes in appetite or weight recently.
Patient's leg puffiness has been consistent and not worse in the morning or evening.
Patient has not noticed any changes in the color or temperature of his legs.
Patient has not noticed any swelling in his ankles or feet.
Patient has not noticed any changes in his ability to perform physical activities or any new symptoms since his last follow-up.
Patient experiences dizziness within a few seconds of standing up, lasting a few seconds to a minute.
Patient's blood pressure when lying down is around 120/80 mmHg.
Patient's blood pressure when standing up for 1 minute is around 105/70 mmHg.
Patient has not experienced any falls or near-falls due to dizziness.
Patient has not made any specific lifestyle changes to manage dizziness.
Patient stands up slowly to manage dizziness.
Patient has not noticed any lightheadedness, fainting spells, or changes in vision or balance other than dizziness when standing up quickly.
